title: PXAPI client report model v1
description: The customer projection of one Analysis Run (Confluence 39846055 §12): the business-language content from which the customer report is rendered, and nothing else. Its property list is the leakage boundary: no member of this document, at any depth, carries internal analysis vocabulary, and no reason code, confidence, coverage figure or method detail reaches the customer. Every lever traces back to at least one product-diagnosis recommendation. A presented index is either SHOWN with a number or WITHHELD with no number and no reason text; a withheld index is never a finding about the website. At least one lever and at least one closing action are always present; an empty scores or charts array means nothing of that kind is presented, never that anything was assessed or not assessed.

run_id.description: Required. The Analysis Run this customer projection belongs to.

generated_at.description: Required. When the customer projection was generated.

projection_version.description: Required. The version of the projection rules that produced this content, so that reports from different runs are comparable only when the projection is the same.

language.description: Required. The language of every text in this document as a two-letter ISO 639-1 code; the rendered report uses the same language.

company_name.description: Required, nullable. The name of the business as it appears in the report; null if and only if the business is not named in the report.

headline.description: Required. The single-line headline of the report, in business language.

summary.description: Required. The summary of the report for the entrepreneur, in business language.

levers.description: Required. The business levers presented to the customer, in presentation order. At least one is required: a report without a lever is invalid, so an empty array is rejected.

scores.description: Required. The indices presented to the customer, in presentation order. An empty array means no index is presented; it never means anything was withheld — that is stated per index.

charts.description: Required. The charts the rendered report embeds, in presentation order. An empty array means the report has no chart.

closing_actions.description: Required. The closing calls to action for the entrepreneur, in presentation order. At least one is required: a report without a closing action is invalid, so an empty array is rejected.

lever_id.description: Required. The stable identity of this lever within the report.

title.description: Required. A single-line title of the lever, in business language.

business_impact.description: Required. What the lever means for the business, in business language.

next_steps.description: Required. The concrete next steps for this lever, in order. At least one is required: a lever without a next step is invalid, so an empty array is rejected.

recommendation_refs.description: Required. The recommendation_ids of the product-diagnosis recommendations this lever presents. At least one is required: a lever without a recommendation behind it is invalid, so an empty array is rejected.

index_id.description: Required. The index_id of the scorecard index this entry presents.

label.description: Required. The customer-facing label of the index, in business language.

state.description: Required. Whether a number is presented for this index. SHOWN: the value is presented. WITHHELD: the index is presented without a number and without any reason text; a withheld index is never a finding about the website. No partial or placeholder state exists.

value.description: Required, nullable. The presented value on the 0..100 scale; non-null if and only if state is SHOWN, null if and only if state is WITHHELD. A withheld index carries no number and no reason.

chart_id.description: Required. The stable identity of this chart within the report.

kind.description: Required. The kind of chart (e.g. index_bars, radar, gauge) as an opaque token whose meaning the renderer defines.

data_ref.description: Required. The chart data artifact the renderer draws this chart from.
